This Service Level Agreement is entered into on this 1st day of April 2025, between NexPay Financial Services Limited (hereinafter referred to as the "Provider") and the enterprise client executing the corresponding Service Order Form (hereinafter referred to as the "Client"). The terms herein govern the provision of payment processing, settlement, and reconciliation services through the NexPay Gateway platform.

1. DEFINITIONS

1.1 "Business Day" shall mean a day (other than a Sunday) on which banks in Mumbai are open for general business.

1.2 "Downtime" shall mean the period during which the NexPay Gateway is unavailable for processing transactions, as measured by the Provider's monitoring systems. Scheduled maintenance windows notified to the Client at least 72 hours in advance shall not be counted as Downtime.
(c) any act or omission of the Client, its employees, agents, or contractors, including but not limited to the Client's failure to maintain a suitable internet connection, hardware, or software required for access to the NexPay Gateway;

(d) any third-party service or infrastructure not under the reasonable control of the Provider, including but not limited to public internet connectivity, power supply, or telecommunications services;

(e) any use of the NexPay Gateway in breach of the applicable Service Order Form, the Provider's Acceptable Use Policy, or any other agreement between the parties;

(f) any malicious attack, denial-of-service attack, or security breach that the Provider could not reasonably have prevented or mitigated.

2.5 The parties acknowledge that the Monthly Uptime Percentage is measured on a monthly basis and that the Provider may, at its sole discretion, offer additional service credits or goodwill adjustments in respect of any month in which the uptime commitment is not met, even where such failure is attributable to a cause listed in Clause 2.4.

3. SERVICE CREDIT CALCULATION

3.1 If the Monthly Uptime Percentage for a calendar month falls below the commitment set out in Clause 2.1, the Client shall be entitled to claim a Service Credit in accordance with the following table:

| Monthly Uptime Percentage | Service Credit (% of monthly subscription fee) |
|---------------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| 99.0% to less than 99.9%  | 10%                                            |
| 95.0% to less than 99.0%  | 25%                                            |
| Less than 95.0%           | 50%                                            |

3.2 Service Credits shall be calculated on the basis of the monthly subscription fee applicable to the Client under the relevant Service Order Form. Where the Client has subscribed to annual billing, the monthly subscription fee shall be deemed to be one-twelfth of the annual fee.

3.3 Service Credits shall be applied as a deduction against the Client's next invoice. In the event that the Client is not subject to any further invoicing, the Provider shall refund the Service Credit amount to the Client within thirty (30) days of the issuance of the credit note.

The contract documents specify the SLA sla_uptime_percentage as 99.9 percent. Record status: current.

3.4 The total Service Credits issued in any calendar year shall not exceed fifty percent (50%) of the annual subscription fee paid by the Client in that year.

3.5 The Client must submit a claim for Service Credits in writing within fifteen (15) Business Days of the end of the calendar month in which the uptime commitment was not met. Claims submitted after this period shall be deemed to have been waived.

3.6 Service Credits are the Client's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure by the Provider to meet the uptime commitment set out in Clause 2.1.

4. REPORTING AND VERIFICATION

4.1 The Provider shall publish on the NexPay status page a monthly summary of the uptime achieved for the Gateway, along with any scheduled maintenance windows and significant incidents.

4.2 Upon the Client's reasonable request, the Provider shall provide a detailed uptime report, including the start and end timestamps of any Downtime events, the duration of such events, and the cause of the unavailability.

4.3 The Client may appoint an independent third-party auditor, subject to the Provider's prior written consent, to verify the uptime calculations. Such consent shall not be unreasonably withheld. Any such audit shall be conducted during normal business hours and shall not unreasonably disrupt the Provider's operations.

4.4 The Client shall bear the costs of any audit conducted pursuant to Clause 4.3 unless the audit reveals that the Provider's reported uptime was inaccurate by more than 0.1 percentage points for the audited month, in which case the Provider shall reimburse the Client for the reasonable costs of the audit.
